**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Price action was very bullish across the precious metals complex in the second half of January. Despite the troubles of the European economy, the Dollar weakened throughout, allowing all the major metals to make very healthy gains. On the 25th, the US Federal Open Market Committee gave hints that QE3 could yet happen and indicated that interest rates would remain low for longer than previously expected. Gold jumped by $60 an ounce and all the other metals followed it higher. Given the currencydriven nature of most of the gains made so far this month, any change to a weaker Euro and a stronger US Dollar could pose significant headwinds making further price gains harder to achieve. • All four of the major precious metals recorded significant increases in net long speculator positions on the futures exchanges in the week to the 24th of January, suggesting a degree of positivity is developing amongst investors. Given the price movements since that date, we expect the next Commitment of Traders report to reveal heavy short covering has since taken place. • ETF flows were positive for gold, palladium and platinum in the week to the 27th of January. Inflows into the gold funds suggested a certain degree of risk aversion while buying in platinum and palladium seemed to demonstrate outright bullishness. The selling seen from the silver ETFs suggest that the recent gains in the silver price have been won without significant help from the physical market. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **30 January 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **30 January 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 24 January 2012; ETF data to 27 January 2012.** ### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Nonetheless, during this period, gold had quietly moved from an opening $1,565 to trade in a range of $1,640 to $1,670 from the 17th to the 20th of January. A weakening Dollar provided ample encouragement for investors to buy gold and drive the price steadily higher. The price challenged $1,680 on the 23rd but found resistance there and fell back below $1,660 on the 25th. The major news, though, came later that day. The FOMC revealed that it expected US interest rates to stay at a low level until at least 2014, longer than the market had previously expected. The associated hint that QE3 could yet occur added further energy and gold surged to $1,710 that day. The price has firmed further since despite a lack of physical interest from China (due to the closure of the Shanghai Gold Exchange for Chinese New Year), reaching a high of $1,740 early on the 30th before falling back to $1,719. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Jan 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

TOCOM positioning shortened by 110,000 ounces. - A little over half a million ounces of gold were added to global ETF positions in the week to the 27th of January. Total holdings climbed to near– record levels of almost 70 million ounces. - The silver price has risen by more than 15 per cent since the start of the year in moving from its initial sub-$28 to over $33. The two major movements in recent weeks were driven by different factors. On the 20th of January, the addition of ten million ounces to the Sprott silver bullion fund prompted a move from $30.5 to $32 per ounce. At the start of the following week, the silver price softened, drifting back below $32 until the FOMC revealed its views on the likely trajectory of US interest rates. Their comments suggested that rates will be maintained at low levels for longer than previously expected and indicated that further quantitative easing could yet take place. Most asset prices ripped higher on this news, with silver leaping to $33 before pressing on to nearly $34 on the 27th. It has since fallen back to $33.30. So far this year, silver has outperformed gold in price terms. We believe this price strength is not currently supported by fundamentals but has instead been driven by investor interest. - Net long speculative silver positions on COMEX climbed by 20.6 million ounces in the week to the 24th of January. The increased long interest came in the futures market where investors covered short positions and added to their longs. Given the sharp move higher since that point, we expect t

he next Commitment of Traders report to show substantial short covering. Overall exposure is still only 143 million ounces, relatively low by recent standards in the silver market. - ETF flows in silver were once again negative in the week to the 27th of January with almost two million ounces of net disinvestment sending total global holdings down to 452 million ounces. Given this negative demand from the ETF sector, we find the price performance of silver last week to be a little surprising. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **30 January 2012** ## **Platinum CFTC data to 24 January 2012; ETF data to 27 January 2012.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

- Gold’s premium over platinum has narrowed this year, falling from over $200 per ounce to roughly $120. Given the positive price performance of gold, this demonstrates the remarkable strength of the platinum price. With the Chinese and Hong Kong markets out for the Chinese New Year, some price weakness might have been expected but ETF buying came to the rescue. The more important issue was the weakening US Dollar which allowed many commodity prices to rise. Platinum climbed from $1,500 on the 17th to $1,550 on the 25th. When the FOMC indicated that it expected to maintain low US interest rates until late-2014, gold roared higher. Platinum followed a little more hesitantly but still gained $40 that day and a similar amount on

the 26th. The price peaked at $1,622 on the 27th but has since fallen back to just above the $1,600 level. If the Euro weakens in the next week, it will be interesting to see what levels platinum can hold. - The bullishness in the platinum market continued in the week to the 24th of January. Net long speculative positions increased by 108,000 ounces to 1.28 million ounces, their fourth consecutive weekly increase. Although gold positions are much larger than platinum positions, investors are adding more quickly (in percentage terms) to their long platinum exposure, helping to explain why the gold-platinum spread has been narrowing. - Platinum ETF holdings have increased in each of the first four weeks of 2012, with investors having added a modest 36,000 ounces in aggregate so far, lifting the total weight of metal held in ETF vaults to 1.44 million ounces. Unlike in palladium, all of the buying this week was seen in Europe with the three largest European funds all seeing net inflows of metal. Given this overt bullishness from European investors, will North American investors follow suit in the coming weeks? 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **30 January 2012** ## **Palladium CFTC data to 24 January 2012; ETF data to 27 January 2012.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Although palladium started 2012 somewhat weakly, it has since rallied from the lows of $615 to challenge $700 - unsuccessfully - before softening to

a morning fix of $681 on the 30th of January. Along with the other precious metals, palladium benefited from a weak US Dollar throughout the second half of the month. With sentiment over Europe seemingly improving (in the short term at least), the prospects for physical demand for the more industrial precious metals improved a little, adding a little more positive sentiment. The return of ETF buying was helpful too in driving palladium to higher levels. The platinum:palladium price ratio has traded in a range from 2.4 to 2.2 since the start of December and the fate of both metals seems linked in the short term. 

- Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX increased by 273,000 ounces in the week to the 24th of January, the largest weekly increase since June last year. Total positioning climbed from 550,000 ounces to 823,000 ounces as new outright longs were added and short covering was seen as well. Futures actions last week are likely to have been less dramatic but if the price can move above $700, we could see further substantial long interest developing. 



- ETF investors added 42,000 ounces of palladium to their holdings in the week to the 27th of January, taking them to a total of 1.77 million ounces. Buying was seen in the two Swiss funds and in the US fund, suggesting a broad return of interest from this sector. The total weekly amount of buying was the largest since April 2011 and was the third successive week of net inflows, suggesting that sentiment might be changing, adding to the prospects for price appreciation this year.
